en: vt. to defeat a person, country or enemy and take control of them; to succeed in dealing with a difficulty; vi. to win a victory
ex: The army conquered the neighboring country in just three months.
軍隊在短短三個月內征服了鄰國。

en: vi. to be formed or made up of particular parts; to have something as its main or only quality; to agree with something
ex: The team consists of ten players and one coach.
這支隊伍由十位球員和一位教練組成。

en: vt. to build something such as a building or road; to form something by combining parts or ideas; to draw a geometric figure; n. an idea or theory formed in the mind
ex: They plan to construct a new bridge across the river.
他們計畫在河上建造一座新橋。

en: n. the process of building something such as a house, bridge or road; a building or structure that has been built; the way that something is built; the interpretation of a sentence or phrase
ex: The construction of the new airport will take five years.
新機場的興建將需要五年。

en: n. a person who gives professional advice on a particular subject; a doctor who is an expert in a particular area of medicine; a person who asks for advice from someone
ex: She works as a financial consultant for several companies.
她擔任好幾家公司的財務顧問。

en: n. a person who buys goods or services for their own use; a person or thing that uses a product or resource
ex: Consumers are becoming more aware of healthy food choices.
消費者越來越注重健康的食物選擇。

en: n. something such as a box, bottle or bowl used for holding or storing things; a large metal box used for transporting goods on ships and trains
ex: Put the leftover food in a plastic container.
把剩菜放進塑膠容器裡。

en: n. the things that are contained in something; the subject matter of a book, speech or website; the amount of something in a substance; a. satisfied with what you have; vt. to make someone feel satisfied
ex: The website content is updated every week.
網站內容每週更新。

en: n. a competition in which people try to win a prize; an argument about something; vt. to argue against something; to compete for something; vi. to compete for something
ex: She won first prize in the speech contest.
她在演講比賽中得了第一名。

en: a. happening again and again over a period of time; repeated often with short stops in between; continuing without stopping
ex: The continual noise from next door made it hard to sleep.
隔壁不斷傳來的噪音讓人難以入睡。

en: a. completely different from something else; (of a person) stubborn and difficult; n. the opposite of something; adv. in a way that is opposite to something
ex: Contrary to popular belief, the earth is not flat.
與一般認知相反，地球不是平的。

en: vt. to express a thought, feeling or idea so that other people understand it; to carry or transport something from one place to another; to give something to someone legally
ex: She tried to convey her feelings through a letter.
她試著透過一封信傳達她的心意。

en: vt. to make someone believe that something is true; to make someone agree to do something; to persuade someone
ex: She convinced her parents to let her study abroad.
她說服父母讓她出國讀書。

en: vi. to deal successfully with a difficult situation; to be able to manage something; to compete; n. a long loose cloak worn by a priest
ex: She can't cope with the stress of her new job.
她無法應付新工作的壓力。

en: n. a reddish-brown metal used for making wire, pipes and coins; (informal) a police officer; a coin made of copper; a reddish-brown color
ex: Copper is a good conductor of electricity.
銅是良好的電導體。

en: n. a long thin rope or strong string; an electric wire with a plug; a part of the body shaped like a rope; vt. to tie something with a cord
ex: He tied the package with a thick cord.
他用粗繩把包裹綁起來。

en: vi. to be similar to or match something; to exchange letters with someone; to be equal to something; to agree with something
ex: The two accounts of the accident do not correspond.
這兩種對事故的說法不一致。

en: n. the clothes worn by a particular group of people or in a particular period; clothes that people wear to look like a different person or character; a swimming suit
ex: The children wore costumes for the Halloween party.
孩子們穿著服裝參加萬聖節派對。

en: n. a small house in the countryside or a village; a small holiday house; a small house in a rural area
ex: They rented a cottage by the sea for the summer.
他們為暑假租了一間海邊小屋。

en: n. a long flat surface in a shop, bank or bar where customers are served; a small round object used in board games; a machine used for counting; vt. to oppose or reply to something; a. opposite; adv. in the opposite direction
ex: She waited at the counter to pay for her groceries.
她在櫃檯等著結帳買雜貨。

en: n. polite behavior that shows respect for other people; a polite action or remark; a favor or act of kindness
ex: He opened the door for her as a courtesy.
他出於禮貌為她開門。

en: n. a narrow break in the surface of something; a sudden loud sharp noise; a quick, sharp hit; v. to break without dividing into pieces; to make a sudden loud noise; a. very good or skillful
ex: There's a crack in the cup, so don't use it.
杯子有一條裂縫，別用它。

en: n. a skill that needs a lot of practice and experience; a job or activity that requires skill with the hands; a boat, ship or aircraft; vt. to make something carefully using skill
ex: Pottery is an ancient craft practiced around the world.
陶藝是世界各地都有的古老手藝。

en: n. the ability to produce original ideas or things; the ability to think of new and interesting ways of doing things; the quality of being creative
ex: Children show great creativity when they play.
孩子玩耍時展現出極大的創造力。

en: vi. to move slowly and quietly with the body close to the ground; to move slowly and carefully; (of a plant) to grow along a surface; n. a slow movement; (slang) an unpleasant person
ex: The cat crept silently towards the bird.
貓悄悄地朝鳥爬過去。

en: a. expressing disapproval or finding fault; extremely important or necessary; very serious or dangerous; (of a physical point) at which a change takes place
ex: Water is critical to the survival of all living things.
水對所有生物的生存都至關重要。

en: n. a statement that expresses disapproval of someone or something; the act of judging the good and bad qualities of something; a written discussion of the good and bad points of a book, film or play
ex: The politician faced a lot of criticism for his decision.
那位政治人物的決定招致許多批評。

en: n. behavior that causes pain or suffering to someone, especially in a deliberate way; an act of cruelty; behavior that is very unkind
ex: The organization fights against cruelty to animals.
這個組織致力於對抗虐待動物。

en: a. (of food) firm and making a loud noise when you bite it; making a noise like that of something being crushed; (of food) pleasantly hard
ex: The crunchy apples taste fresh and sweet.
這些脆脆的蘋果吃起來新鮮又甜。

en: n. a solid shape with six equal square sides; a small block of something such as ice or sugar; the result of multiplying a number by itself twice; vt. to cut something into small cubes; to raise a number to the third power
ex: He dropped an ice cube into his drink.
他把一塊冰塊丟進飲料裡。

en: a. clever in a way that tricks other people; showing skill in deceiving others; (old use) charming and attractive; n. skill in tricking people
ex: The fox is known as a cunning animal.
狐狸被認為是狡猾的動物。

en: n. a strong desire to know or learn about something; an unusual and interesting object or thing; an unusual fact
ex: Curiosity killed the cat, as the saying goes.
俗話說，好奇心殺死貓。

en: n. a soft bag filled with a soft material, used to make a seat or bed more comfortable; something that reduces the effect of a shock or loss; vt. to protect someone from something unpleasant; to soften the effect of a blow
ex: She put a cushion on the chair to make it more comfortable.
她在椅子上放了一個墊子讓它更舒服。

en: a. slightly wet, often in an unpleasant way; n. wetness in the air or on surfaces; vt. to make something slightly wet; to reduce the strength of something
ex: The basement was cold and damp.
地下室又冷又潮濕。

en: v. to announce something officially; to state something clearly and firmly; to tell customs officers about the goods you have bought abroad; to make something known
ex: The country declared independence in 1948.
該國在 1948 年宣布獨立。

en: n. the act of losing a battle or competition; a failure to succeed at something; vt. to win against someone in a battle or competition; to prevent something from succeeding
ex: The team suffered a heavy defeat in the final.
球隊在決賽遭到慘敗。

en: n. the act of protecting something from attack; the defenders in a team game; the things that protect someone or something; an argument used to prove that someone is not guilty
ex: The country spends a lot of money on national defense.
該國在國防上花費很多經費。

en: a. able to be protected from attack; able to be supported by good arguments; able to be defended
ex: Her position on the issue is quite defensible.
她對這個議題的立場相當站得住腳。

en: a. easily damaged or broken; fine and soft in appearance; needing careful handling; (of food or flavor) pleasantly mild and subtle; (of a situation) requiring tact
ex: Be careful with the delicate glass.
小心處理這個精緻易碎的玻璃。

en: vi. to leave a place, especially at the start of a journey; to do something different from what is usual or expected; (formal) to die
ex: The train departs from platform three at noon.
火車中午從三號月台出發。
